title: Container Bookings: containers on which a change-of-destination fee is charged
content:
## Rule
For a change of port of discharge on a Container Bookings booking:
- On a tier whose change of destination is not allowed, a change of port of discharge is never accepted, so it has no chargeable containers and bears no fee.
- The fee is charged only on the containers the line will carry. Containers covered by the booking's dangerous-goods acceptance that the line has rejected are not carried and are left out.
- The chargeable containers are therefore the booking's container count less the container count of that rejected dangerous-goods acceptance, never below zero; when the booking has no rejected acceptance, nothing is subtracted.
- A booking on which more than one dangerous-goods acceptance has been rejected falls outside these rules, because its chargeable containers are not defined by them.

The rejection and its container count are read from the dangerous-goods acceptance record of the booking.

## Cases (hypothetical counts)
| Tier allows a change of destination | Booking containers | Rejected dangerous-goods acceptance | Chargeable containers |
|---|---|---|---|
| no | 10 | none | 0 |
| yes | 10 | none | 10 |
| yes | 10 | one, covering 3 containers | 7 |
| yes | 10 | one, covering 12 containers | 0 (never below zero) |
| yes | 10 | two rejected acceptances | not defined by these rules |

*All figures are hypothetical inputs, for illustration only.*

## Points of judgement
**An acceptance is approved rather than rejected.** Only a rejected acceptance takes containers out; an approved one subtracts nothing.
